screen: #/run/start/purpose (full, fixture); the same cards are drawn on the connected /start Purpose step
title: The focused Purpose card is drawn exactly like the selected, unfocused one: the focus outline is declared but never painted.
expected: D-34: every focusable element shows a focus indicator on keyboard focus (focus ring 2px, 2px offset, 3:1); no outline-none without a replacement. D-35: operable by keyboard.
actual: RadioButton in PurposeCards sets outline-none and adds outline-2 outline-offset-2 outline-brand only while isFocusVisible. Tailwind's outline-2 sets a width only, so the computed outline-style stays none (outline 'none 2px', data-focus-visible=true). Tab and the arrow keys always land on the selected card, so the 2px ring the reader sees is the selected-state ring (ring-2 ring-brand). Screenshots of the card unfocused and focused are byte-identical (same SHA-1). The connected Start page uses the same PurposeCards and shows the same computed style (outline-style none on the focused label).
suggested_change: Give the focus-visible branch an outline-solid (or a ring distinct from the selected ring), for example isFocusVisible && 'outline-2 outline-solid outline-offset-2 outline-focus'.

title: Confirming the Submit dialog removes the Submit button and leaves keyboard focus on the document body; the new 'Run started' panel is not announced or focused.
expected: D-38: on close, focus returns to the opener or, if the opener has gone, to a logical place. D-43: a status change is announced without moving focus (the live region exists before the change).
actual: Escape, the scrim and Cancel return focus to the Submit button (checked). Confirm closes the dialog and sets window.location.hash; the Start step is replaced by the Started step, so the opener is gone and document.activeElement becomes body (next Tab starts at Skip to content). The Run started alert (role=status) is inserted together with the new page, not into an existing region, so a screen reader gets no announcement.
suggested_change: After onConfirm, move focus to the Run started alert title (tabIndex -1) or to its first link.

screen: #/run/start/purpose, confirm, start, started and #/run/activity/finished, failed, capped, rejected, interrupted, unreadable (full, fixture)
title: Only 7 of 17 populated static run pages say they are a saved example; the Start step offers a 'Start a paid run?' dialog and the next page says 'Run started' although nothing is started or spent.
expected: D-17 (the synthetic test mode spends nothing and is labelled); D-15 (a synthetic case is allowed only where labelled); CM-087 and CT-032/CT-033 (Submit is explicit, and a test run is labelled).
actual: The notice 'Not available here: this page shows a saved example and is not connected to the run service' (NOT_CONNECTED) is drawn only beside disabled controls: Documents and More context steps, and Stop run on live runs. The Purpose, Confirm, Start and Started steps and the finished, failed, capped, rejected, interrupted and unreadable run pages carry no such line. On Start, the dialog reads 'This run can spend up to USD 20.00 ... what it has spent cannot be taken back', its action 'Start run, up to USD 20.00' moves to #/run/start/started, which reads 'Run started. 13 modules will read 4 documents ...' and 'You can close this page. The run carries on'. Start.tsx documents that nothing is sent, but no sentence on screen says so. The run pages draw a real issuer name with invented spend and times.
suggested_change: Draw the saved-example line once, in the shared frame of every populated run page and step (and name it in the dialog and on Run started), instead of only beside disabled controls.

title: Every cap the static pages draw for a 'Full credit review' is USD 20.00; the Full pathway's cap is USD 25.
expected: CM-084, CT-013, CT-021 and retired R-09 (Lite 15, Full 25, Deep 40, the five purpose pathways 20; docs/rulings/2026-11-15-pathway-tiers-and-caps.md); D-15 (a figure is the real figure); D-17.
actual: Readiness ('USD 0.00 of USD 20.00', every step), the Confirm row 'Spending cap USD 20.00', the Start paragraph, the Submit label 'Submit, spend up to USD 20.00', the dialog text and action, the Run started text, and every run's cap bar and alerts ('The run reached its USD 20.00 cap') all read 20.00 beside the label 'Full credit review'. The connected Start page shows USD 25.00 for the same pathway. The app draws the strings as the slice gives them (verified: 447 figure checks against web/fixtures/run.json, 0 mismatches), so the wrong cap is in the fixture, the only source these screens have.
suggested_change: Change the run fixture's cap to the pathway's cap (25 for Full) in every readiness bar, summary row, dialog, label and run record; Medium rather than High because the figure is fixture data, not computed, and the shipped data.js holds no run slice.

title: The Purpose step offers four mock purposes, not the eight pathways: no Lite, Deep, Relative Value, Covenant & Refinancing, Distressed & Restructuring or Portfolio Decision; 'Event review' is not a pathway and 'Long label review' is test copy.
expected: CM-084 (eight pathway choices, Lite first, Full selected on opening, each with its cap in USD); CT-012 to CT-019; D-15 (no placeholder content).
actual: Radios, in order: Full credit review (selected), Earnings update, Event review, Long label review. The descriptions carry no cap per pathway. The fourth card reads 'A synthetic purpose whose module label is long, to show that the label wraps.' The Full card's chip reads '13 modules' where CT-013 lists 15 entries. The connected app shows all eight with Lite first and Full selected, so the two surfaces disagree.
suggested_change: Replace the fixture's purposes with the eight pathway cards (Lite first, Full selected, cap shown on each) and keep the long-label case in a test fixture that is not drawn as a product choice.

title: Choosing another purpose changes nothing: Confirm and Start still say 'Full credit review, 13 modules', and the choice is lost on Previous or reload.
expected: Effect the screen implies: the radio sets the purpose the run will use (Purpose step: 'The purpose decides which modules run'); a state that is set is read (check 5).
actual: Selecting 'Earnings update' and pressing Next lands on Confirm with 'Purpose Full credit review' and 'Modules 13'; going Previous shows 'Full credit review' selected again. Purpose keeps the choice in useState and the Next link is a fixed href, so no other component reads it. The step gives no sign that the choice is not kept (the More context step says 'Not saved here', this one does not).
suggested_change: Either say on the Purpose step that the choice is not kept in a saved example, or disable the radios as the Documents controls are; do not leave live-looking radios that discard the choice.

screen: #/run/activity/<run> for finished, failed, capped, interrupted (full), breadcrumb 'Runs'
title: The 'Runs' breadcrumb opens #/run, which draws the one run the slice calls current (the running one), not a list of runs; no static page lists runs in progress, the queue or ended runs.
expected: CM-090 (Run activity shows runs in progress and the queue, and runs that ended without a report); a link named 'Runs' leads to runs.
actual: From a failed, capped, finished or interrupted run, 'Runs' goes to the TransDigm 'Running' page. The other runs are reachable only by typing their address or from a link in an alert. Nothing on the static surface shows more than one run at a time. (The connected /runs page is a list; this is the static twin.)
suggested_change: Make 'Runs' open an index of the slice's runs (state, pathway, as-of), or drop the breadcrumb word; the slice already holds every run.

screen: #/run/activity/finished, failed, capped, interrupted; #/run/start/started 'Back to the library' (full, fixture)
title: 'Open the library' and 'Open what finished' go to the Library home (#/), which does not hold the run's issuer, so the finished work cannot be reached.
expected: A link named 'Open what finished' opens the finished modules of that run; 'its library appears under TransDigm Group' (Started.tsx).
actual: All four hrefs are '#/'; the Library home draws Halden Aerostructures, Corvane Packaging, Tessaly Foods, Ardenne Cable and Lumora Health, and no TransDigm Group, the issuer of every run fixture. The stage 0 note that run-activity pages link to #/library/transdigm/... does not reproduce: no S6 page holds such an href (0 found); those links are in web/fixtures/model.json (Model section). The slice reader only requires an href that starts with '#/', so the writer is not checked against an issuer that exists.
suggested_change: Point the links at the run's own library address (#/library/<issuer>/<run>/overview) and add that issuer to the library fixture, or check in the slice reader that the target exists.

title: 'Try again' links to the page it is on: pressing it changes nothing and gives no feedback.
expected: A control named Try again re-reads the run record and shows the result or a message (D-31: errors carry an action).
actual: href '#/run/activity/unreadable' equals the current hash; nothing re-reads (the data is a script loaded once) and the page text is identical afterwards.
suggested_change: In a saved example, draw the control disabled with the NOT_CONNECTED reason, as Stop run is, or remove it; in the connected app it should re-request.

screen: #/run/activity/many-modules at 390 px (full, fixture); #/run/activity/running at 1440 px with an unbroken label
title: A run's label chip cannot wrap: the fixture's own long label ('Full credit review with every optional module and a late cut-off') is cut off at 390 px, and one unbroken label pushes Stop run off the page at 1440 px.
expected: D-32 (long text wraps in full; a qualification is never truncated); D-42 (reflow at narrow widths).
actual: The chip is a Badge (whitespace-nowrap). At 390 px its right edge is at 459 px, past the 390 px viewport; the main region clips it, so the reader sees '... and a lat'. At 1440 px a label of 160 unbroken characters moves the header actions to x = 1679, outside the viewport (the Stop run button and its reason are not visible). Spaced long labels wrap correctly in the headings, alerts, feed and module rows (checked with 4x-long strings).
suggested_change: Let run labels wrap (whitespace-normal, max-w-full, break-words) in the PageHeader badge row; the nowrap is in the X1 Badge, so the change belongs in the label row.

title: The Run start stepper's completed steps are not buttons on the static page, so a step cannot be revisited from the stepper.
expected: CM-083 (Run start has a stepper whose completed steps are buttons); the connected stepper does this ('Go back to Documents' is a button there).
actual: StartPage draws <Stepper step={draft.step} /> with no onSelect, so Stepper renders every step as a span: 4 of 4 completed steps on the Start step, 0 buttons. Previous and Next links still move one step.
suggested_change: Pass onSelect that sets window.location.hash to the draft of that step, using the draft ids the slice already carries (or state in the row that the static stepper is read-only).

title: The review step shows a count of modules and none of the rest of the review sheet: no module names, no left-out modules, no run limits or decisions, no 'Changes' comparison row, no web-lookup statement; approval is a link, not an approval.
expected: CM-086 (modules plain-named, left-out modules, run limits and decisions needed, the Changes row naming the earlier run or 'first run', the web-lookup statement, an approval); CT-028, CT-029, CT-030, CT-031; D-17 (what will not be done is shown before Submit).
actual: The three groups are Issuer, Documents and Run ('Modules 13' only). 'Approve summary' is an <a> to #/run/start/context and the Approval badge ('Awaiting your approval') never changes. The probe finds 0 of the 6 review-sheet parts. The confirm draft is a list of read-only label/value rows, so limits to decide and an approval control cannot be expressed even with real data.
suggested_change: Extend the confirm draft with the review-sheet parts the connected ReviewSheet draws, or record that the static review step is a reduced snapshot.

title: The Start step's Submit button is whitespace-nowrap and 307 px wide, so the card is wider than the viewport: 15 px past the right gutter at 390 px, and at 320 px the text is cut off and main scrolls sideways.
expected: D-42 (content reflows to one column at 320 CSS px without two-direction scrolling); D-26 (sibling screens share gutters).
actual: At 390 px the Start card spans x = 16..389 while every other card spans 16..374. At 320 px the card spans 16..389, main has scrollWidth 389 > clientWidth 320, the stepper's fifth marker and the end of every line are clipped, and the paid action extends to x = 356.
suggested_change: Let the Submit button wrap or fill its container below the 620 px container width (w-full, whitespace-normal).

title: The run alerts offer 'Review and resume' and 'Review and start again', but the control matrix says no page control for resuming exists and that a resume is a launcher relaunch into the same folder.
expected: CT-038 and harmony-report H-15 (no resume control found; resume only at the folder's own cap); AGENTS.md (CP-OS resumes affected work).
actual: Both links go to #/run/start/start, the Submit step, and the alert text says 'Resuming goes through Start and asks before it spends'. A reader is told a resume exists.
suggested_change: none: the owner decides whether the app offers a resume or start-again action (H-15).

title: Run activity shows module states only: plan, delivery and library admission have no state of their own, so a run whose modules finished cannot be told from one that was delivered and admitted.
expected: CM-089 (plan, execution, delivery and library admission have distinct states), CM-117 and CM-204 (end-to-end execution and delivery, I5 steps with S1).
actual: The slice (slice-activity.ts) has no field for them and the 'Finished' badge is the only run state. The connected page also draws only the module list and a 'Run' feed line 'Report delivered'.
suggested_change: none: the owner decides whether delivery and admission states are drawn (the matrix is ahead of both surfaces).

title: The cap is not named on Run activity: the figure is captioned 'Spend' and the bar reads 'USD 7.40 of USD 20.00'.
expected: CM-089 and CM-205 (cap and spend labelled); CT-039; the connected page captions it 'Cap usage' and says '... of USD 25.00 cap usage'.
actual: Summary defaults spendCaption to 'Spend'; the static fixtures' bar labels carry no word 'cap'. 'Cap' appears only in the capped alert and in the Queued and Started feed lines.
suggested_change: Pass spendCaption 'Spend and cap' (or put 'cap' in the bar label) on the static page.

title: Readiness lists 'Model service reachable' as Met on pages that say they are not connected to any service.
expected: D-15 (a figure or state is real or labelled); CT-032/CT-033.
actual: Every draft lists 'Model service reachable' and 'Spending cap set' as met while Documents and More context say the page 'is not connected to the run service'.
suggested_change: Leave the item out of a saved example's readiness list or mark it as not applicable.

screen: all run pages (any state; reached with modified fixture data)
title: The module-code guard in the slice reader (/\bCP-\d/) lets CP-DR, CP-MODEL, CP-L10, CP-OS and lower-case codes through; they are drawn as labels on Run start and Run activity.
expected: D-13 and CM-012/CM-013 (no module code on run start or run activity); slice-read.ts says 'A module code (CP-3) stays off these pages: every string is checked where it is read'.
actual: With a chip 'CP-L10 Credit snapshot', a feed name 'CP-MODEL', a module 'cp-1a Financial analysis' and a readiness item 'Peer set from CP-DR is ready', all four are drawn. The shipped fixture has none, so no screen shows one today.
suggested_change: Widen the guard to /\bCP-[0-9A-Z]/i (and test CP-DR, CP-MODEL, CP-L10, CP-OS).

title: One invalid string makes every run page a bare message that prints the validator's path text, and no run page can be read.
expected: D-31 (no raw error string, errors carry an action); fail() names the path for the developer.
actual: A module code in one draft's issuer turns Run start and Run activity into 'This part of the library could not be read' followed by 'run.drafts[0].issuer: expected no module code', with no icon, alert or action. The message comes from slice-read.ts fail(); App.tsx (S1) draws it.
suggested_change: Draw the reader message inside the kit alert with a next action, and keep the path text under a details line for the person who maintains the data.

title: A value written as an empty string is accepted by the reader and drawn as a blank cell; only null draws 'n.a.'.
expected: D-14 (a missing value is 'n.a.', never an empty cell); Row.value comment 'null draws n.a.'.
actual: strOrNull and Figure.value accept '': Spend and Elapsed draw empty big figures and the Confirm row 'Name' an empty value cell. The probe reads the figure cells as ['', '5 of 13', ''].
suggested_change: Treat a blank string as missing: reject it in the reader or draw <Missing /> for it.

title: Text is drawn below 13 px in six places: 12 px captions, step notes, times, module chips and the upload hint, and 9 px on the file-type label.
expected: D-30 (nothing written here below 13 px; caption 13/18). The config.json exceptions cover one mockup file only.
actual: text-xs (12 px): Stepper note, Summary caption, Feed time, Purpose module chip, Documents upload hint; text-[9px] on the PDF and XLSX label of each file row. Probe lists 15 distinct strings on five pages.
suggested_change: Use the caption token (13/18) for these, and keep the file-type label inside the icon at 13 px or draw it as an icon.

title: Spacing and sizes off the 4/8/12/16/20/24/32 ladder: gap-7 (28 px) between Confirm groups, 6 px and 2 px gaps, and fixed 38 px, 27 px, 18 px and 9 px values on the file icon and alert rings.
expected: D-26 (spacing steps from the ladder; no p-[13px]-style literals); D-30.
actual: Confirm.tsx gap-7; gap-1.5, pt-1.5 and mt-1.5 in ModuleSteps, Context and Documents; mt-0.5 and gap-0.5; Documents.tsx h-[38px] w-[27px] left-[7px] top-[18px] rounded-[2px] text-[9px]; RunAlert after:size-[38px].
suggested_change: Use ladder steps (gap-8, gap-2) and tokenise the file-icon and ring sizes.

title: The Readiness panel nests three bordered surfaces and its item boxes have the same radius as the panel around them.
expected: D-21 (no cards inside cards; every list item in its own bordered box is the failing example); D-23 (a nested element has a smaller radius than its container).
actual: Measured: aside 28 px radius with shadow, ItemGroup section 20 px (surface-subtle), each item 20 px with its own border. The connected StartReadiness draws the same facts as hairline-divided rows (no nested boxes), so the two surfaces also differ (D-26).
suggested_change: Draw the items as rows divided by hairlines, as the connected panel does, and reuse one component.

title: The same FileCheck02 featured icon is drawn on every purpose card; it says nothing the title does not.
expected: D-20 (no decorative icons that carry no meaning; an icon beside every item is the failing pattern).
actual: Each of the four (connected: eight) cards starts with an identical 'brand' featured icon plus the title.
suggested_change: Drop the repeated icon, or use it only on the selected card.

title: The upload hint lists PDF, DOCX, HTML or XLSX; the reader also accepts CSV, TXT, MD, JSON and JSONL, and the connected page names no types.
expected: CT-006 (Excel and CSV files are inputs); src/deploy_workflow/owners/cpos_launch.py SOURCE_SUFFIXES (.pdf .htm .html .docx .txt .md .xlsx .csv .json .jsonl).
actual: Documents.tsx hard-codes 'PDF, DOCX, HTML or XLSX, up to 50 MB each'; a CSV an analyst is allowed to upload is not named.
suggested_change: Say 'Up to 50 MB per file' as the connected page does, or list every accepted type.

title: On the shipped build every run page is the single line 'No run data in this library': no sentence says why or what to do, and the link to start a run is absent.
expected: D-31 (empty state: featured icon, title, one sentence and where it exists the next action); CM-036 (activity with no runs says so).
actual: All 22 addresses show the featured icon and one heading; the fixture variant of the same case ('No run to watch') has a sentence and a 'Start a run' button.
suggested_change: Add one sentence ('This library holds no run records') and a link to the Library.

title: The Documents step cannot be completed: Next says 'Replace or remove the unreadable file to continue', while Replace file, Remove and the drop zone (which still reads 'or drag and drop') are all disabled.
expected: CT-006 (the user adds, removes or carries documents); a reason that tells the reader to act must name an action that exists.
actual: All nine file controls are disabled; the reason text is a visible line below the drop zone. The drop zone has no drop handler, so dropping a file on the page falls to the browser's default (not exercised, see Not verified).
suggested_change: Say in the Next reason that the page is a saved example, and drop the words 'or drag and drop' while the zone is inert.

screen: #/run/start/* after Next or Previous at 390 px (full, fixture)
title: Moving to another step keeps the previous scroll offset: at 390 px the new step opens with its heading 326 px above the viewport.
expected: D-22 (the first thing on a screen is the first thing seen); WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order after a view change).
actual: On Confirm, scrolled to its end, 'Approve summary' lands on More context with main.scrollTop 635 and the h2 at y = -326; focus stays on the Next link. At 1440 px the offset resets only because the page is short.
suggested_change: Scroll main to the top and move focus to the step heading when the draft changes (the root cause may be the shell's main region, S1).

title: An unreadable file row carries two Remove controls: the icon (named 'Remove <file>') and a text button named only 'Remove'.
expected: D-37 (no two different actions share a generic name; a name says what it removes).
actual: Accessibility tree: button 'Remove Investor presentation, scanned.pdf' and button 'Remove'. Both are disabled, so the pair is not heard in a tab walk, but a screen-reader list of buttons names one generically.
suggested_change: Give the text button the file name (aria-label) or drop the duplicate.

title: Disabled controls are unfocusable, so the reason attached to them with aria-describedby is never reached by Tab.
expected: D-35 (everything is operable and discoverable from the keyboard); D-37.
actual: Tab walk of #/run/start/documents stops at Skip, the rail and Library only: Click to upload, every Remove, Previous and Next are skipped. Stop run on the live pages is skipped the same way. The reason is visible text beside the control, so it is reachable in reading mode.
suggested_change: Use aria-disabled with a focusable button that announces the reason, or place the reason where reading order meets it first.

title: The saved example contradicts itself: the More context textarea is empty but the Start recap says 'One note added'; 'a library appears under TransDigm Group' when the library holds no such issuer; the intro line says 'Nothing is spent before the last step' on the page that follows it.
expected: D-15 (the same figure and fact read the same across a flow); CM-086.
actual: Context draft note is '' while the Start recap row is 'More context: One note added'. Started text: 'its library appears under TransDigm Group when it finishes'. The intro paragraph stays on Run started.
suggested_change: Make the fixture consistent and hide the intro line once the run has started.

title: The review step shows 'Reporting currency USD' as a value read from the documents; CM-088 says neither start page asks for or shows it.
expected: CM-088 and CT-011 (the run's currency is the currency of the source statements; not asked, defaulted or read); retired R-18 (no reporting-currency question).
actual: The row is a read-out, not a question, and the page does not ask for the currency; the matrix says 'not shown'. No US$m label or non-USD warning is drawn.
suggested_change: none: the owner decides whether the review sheet may state the currency read from the statements.

title: A 'Stop run' button is drawn (disabled) on every live run page, but no control-matrix row or ruling gives the analyst a Stop.
expected: control-matrix.csv has CT-039 (stop at the cap, automatic) and no row for a user stop; harmony-report H-15 lists only resume and retry as gaps.
actual: Button 'Stop run' (disabled, described by the NOT_CONNECTED reason) on six addresses (clickables.jsonl lines for S6).
suggested_change: none: the owner decides whether a Stop is part of the product; if so the matrix needs a row.

screen: all static run pages (full, empty, error)
title: Parts of the static run screens that no matrix row accounts for: Readiness panel, the More context free-text step, run header chips (pathway, as-of) and status badge, the activity feed, the Elapsed figure, the unreadable-activity state, the not-found and no-run empty states, the saved-example notice, the Approval badge and the Run started panel.
expected: Brief check 4 (list what the screens show that no matrix row accounts for).
actual: None of these has a row in content-matrix.csv or control-matrix.csv with S6 in section_id (CM-083 names the stepper and rows of Documents; CM-089 and CM-090 name module progress and scope).
suggested_change: none: stage 4 decides which rows to add to the matrices.

title: Rows for controls that exist only on the connected page or in the launching environment have no counterpart on the static run screens: the synthetic Submit (CT-033), the Submit retry message (CT-037) and the Teams run cards (CT-042). The R8 question for the Teams POST is still open (harmony-report H-26).
expected: CT-033, CT-037, CT-042; README R8 (only the live model run and CP-DR lookups leave the machine).
actual: None of the S6 screens makes a request to any host but the local machine (0 blocked requests over all addresses, both data variants, and the connected pages opened with proof.serve); the Teams POST is server side, outside these screens. This agent does not settle H-26.
suggested_change: none: the lead or owner settles whether R8 names the Teams card POST as an exception.

title: Dead branches, unread state and duplication in the run files: Readiness' capTitle prop and its 'Unavailable' branch are never used (the connected page has its own StartReadiness), the started draft's position is validated and never drawn, a count text is not checked against its list, ShowAll hard-codes aria-expanded=false, and the 50 MB figure is a literal.
expected: Brief check 5 (state set and never read, props unused, branches no input reaches, duplicated blocks). Measured costs go to stage 6.
actual: (1) Readiness.tsx capTitle and data.cap === null are reached by no caller (StartPage passes neither; slice-start bar() refuses null). (2) The probe reports 'slice fields read and never drawn: 1' (started.position). (3) slice-start.ts unmet() checks only the '0' case, so count '5' over two items is accepted. (4) ModuleSteps ShowAll renders aria-expanded='false' and is removed on press, so no group can be collapsed again. (5) Readiness.tsx and connected StartReadiness.tsx duplicate the panel. (6) Documents.tsx '50 MB' mirrors submissions.py MAX_FILE. (7) No code outside web/fixtures writes a run slice, so on the shipped build these pages are always empty.
suggested_change: Remove the unused prop and branch, draw or drop started.position, share one readiness component.

screen: connected /run/<id> (synthetic, full), drawn by ModuleSteps and Summary
title: The connected Run page says '14 of 14 modules' while the list under 'Modules' holds 15 rows, the last being 'Report'.
expected: D-15 (the same figure reads the same on one screen); CM-089.
actual: Observed on a finished synthetic run (proof.serve, no provider call): progressbar '14 of 14 modules' and 15 list items. Section C1 draws the page; S6 files only render the rows.
suggested_change: none: C1 decides whether 'Report' is a module row or a delivery step.
